newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia privatisation to boost other reforms.
newsitem.headline: Serbia privatisation to boost other reforms.

text.p: Upcoming privatisation in Serbia will give boost to further reforms and help local companies find new business partners, Serbia's Privatisation Minister, Milan Beko, said on Tuesday.

"We are preparing a privatisation law, we talk about ownership and structural changes. It is a way to help companies find new business partners to upgrade their technology and organisation," Beko told a news conference.
Beko insisted the state was there to create the right economic climate.

"The important thing is that we react and that along with creating the right environment for a market economy we also help companies revive their production. The state will retain an important role and should assist companies in their rehabilitation programmes," Beko added.
"It is important to increase production. Once a company increases capacity utilisation, that moment it can start to privatise," Beko told Reuters.
The first Serbian privatisation minister said the final version of the draft privatisation law will be ready in few weeks and offered first to the government and then to the parliament.

"Most companies will be able to embark on privatisation right away, while a few, including the Zastava car producer will first have to restructure and then privatise," the minister said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
